utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are in open session and we had requested from counsel authorities regarding the issue that was raised yesterday afternoon that had to do with the availability to the Prosecutor for use as impeachment purposes a prior statement of the witness. We asked that counsel provide us authorities and indicated that we would hear oral argument this morning. Mr. Tieger, you were the moving party, I suppose, on that issue. Have you presented us with any authorities?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If your Honours please ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: --- if I might argue that matter on behalf of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: May I raise a question, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I think, your Honour, that the matter that has been raised by the Prosecution yesterday is a matter that really attacks the conduct of the Defence in its heart, the way we have dealt with our business so far. We are not ready to argue the matter today. It needs more time for us to prepare for a proper argument in this case. It is a case of principle and we do not feel prepared just one overnight looking into the matter, because there are so many consequences we have to deal with that we cannot argue the matter tomorrow. If I may explain that to you? We have to consider several consequences. First of all, we have to research, not only as we did the English system and the Dutch system, we have to research other systems too. I have a very good feeling that what is in the Dutch system will also be in the other continental systems, but I have not been able to have any confirmation on that. Comparative law is not simply reading the text, one should understand it. The second consequence we want to research is that I want to take advice from the advisory panel which is in the directive on the assignment of the counsel, because I am not convinced that a ruling of your Chamber as you did yesterday will be a matter I can deal with. So I want to take advice on my professional duties in this case, what should I do, according to that panel, because we have to consider our position then. We also have to confer with our client. So far we have had no time to see him. We cannot see him in the evening and yesterday afternoon we had been working on this case. We conferred with the Prosecution. I think we should confer with him. It is an essential issue in this case. We should also confer with him to discuss the ins and outs of a possible interlocutory appeal. That would take time too. In the meantime, he is in custody. We further have to consider very carefully the consequences for our witnesses. There is an enormous impact of any decision on your part for a disclosure by the Defence on our future witnesses, and we cannot simply overnight decide these matters. Under these conditions, we feel we need more time, as we are entitled to under Article 21 of the Statute, to prepare for a proper argument. It is not a simple matter. It is really the heart of the matter. If we step over that line, we have to consider our position.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: How much time do you need, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We need working days. The weekend is for ourselves, we cannot consult others. We would like to argue the matter on Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, in view of the matters raised by Mr. Wladimiroff, we do not oppose his application, but we would also like to take advantage of the time if he is going to have it, so that we will make our presentation at the same time if that was possible.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Tuesday morning at 10 o'clock, Mr. Wladimiroff, is that acceptable with you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I guess so, yes. I am very careful here because we are dependent on people helping us out, providing with what is in the other system. On Monday, I think, we are able to tell you whether we have been able to do this, if not we will tell you. But we think it is a very essential issue we cannot rush. The advisory panel are three persons. They live in separate countries, so I will try to contact them as quick as I can, but they may confer with each other too because we should really take advice here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You probably intend on submitting written materials, I am sure?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, we have translation problems.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will schedule it for Tuesday at 10.00. Will you know Monday? I am really concerned about your witnesses. We are in the middle of one witness now whom we are hearing in closed session. Of course, this issue relates to that witness. If we are going to reserve arguments and reserve a ruling, then that witness will have to continue. That witness will have to be available for continuing cross-examination. We, I imagine, will finish with that witness, although I am not involved, maybe before lunch, certainly by lunch. Then we will go back into closed session, as I understand, to hear another witness, is that not so, following this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I think so, your Honour, we will not call any witness further until this matter has been resolved.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I thought that we would be hearing from witness L ---

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is right. That is another matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: --- next, and that is another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But that is not a witness from whom you have taken a statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So I do not think that that impacts, so we can go forward with L and that will be in closed. How long do you anticipate that you would need for L?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Kay is right. We did not prepare for L because we tried to prepare this, so we need one hour preparation for L and then the cross-examination will take about, let us say, one and a half hour. So we need one hour to prepare and one and a half for cross-examination itself, because we intended to prepare this last night which we could not because we were trying to prepare this argument.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: But you determined that you could not prepare and so you did not go forward to prepare for L, I gather? By then it was probably too late?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We tried to, that is right.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So now you need additional time to prepare for L who will be your next witness after this and he is in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. What we will do, we will just continue with this witness in closed session, W. We will then, depending upon the time, it may fall naturally so that you will have the hour that you need to prepare for L, and then continue with L when you have had the hour. Do you need additional time to prepare for cross-examination of L? Were you working on this motion last night?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no idea what the cross-examination will be about. I think I can only deal with it when we hear the questions that are coming from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are anxious, obviously, as we keep saying to move the trial forward, particularly now you have witnesses here, Mr. Wladimiroff, and I know you do not want them just waiting, but we will give you that time. We will set it for Tuesday at 10.00. If you can advise us on Monday whether you need additional time, then we can set it at Wednesday at 10.00, but keep it in mind that we too are anxious to proceed with the witness. We will hear W and then we will hear L. Then I am concerned, though, about the next witness because the next witness may very well relate to the issue that we are dealing with or, at least, it might arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, we do not think it is good to continue with W unless the matter has been resolved. We are not going to call anyone further until the matter has been resolved. It is a basic matter here and we cannot just go on blind, so we will not agree with any further cross-examination on W.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, may we not continue with W and your other witnesses -- I understand you need additional time for L -- if we reserve this issue of whether or not the Prosecutor is entitled to receive the statement and use it for impeachment purposes of W and any other witnesses? L, we are not going to have that issue, but whoever is the witness following L, and I do not have the list before me, we may have the same issue as we did with W. But if we reserve this issue of whether the Prosecutor is entitled to receive the statement of the witness and use it for impeachment purposes, if we reserve that, then are you ready to go forward with W and, of course, L and then whoever would follow L?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I want to confer on that, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. We may continue under that reservation with W, but we cannot go on with the others because even though under that reservation it will affect our position and we have to know where we stand before we call people that afterwards may be confronted with ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So you can proceed with W with the understanding that we will rule after we hear the arguments, after we receive all of your authorities, as to whether or not that statement may be used for impeachment purposes. Of course, then you will keep W available for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Then you can go forward with L because that is not impacted, assuming you have your hour to prepare that you need for L, but the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We will call no one further until the matter has been resolved, your Honour, so we may continue on W and we shall continue on L.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Let us continue with W and see how much time and when it falls in terms of what you will need for L, then we will advise you regarding the position of the Chamber with respect to the other witnesses. I hear what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for very formal reasons, we cannot make any mistake here, you overruled yesterday twice, is that overruling still standing?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: With respect to the witness statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You overruled questions put to the witness relating to issues we have claimed are privileged. You have overruled our objections relating to the production of any material.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That ruling will not stand until we hear oral argument, so we will withdraw that ruling. As I indicated, I conferred with my fellow Judges and then issued that ruling, but we will withdraw it pending receipt of arguments and the authorities that you will give us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does it also relate to the questions put to the witness related to issues we have claimed to be privileged?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know what questions you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It is on page 4132.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is like we have all been looking at authorities and not had an opportunity to look at the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have it here so I can just show it through the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Since it was in closed, let me take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: It is on two pages.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Tell me what page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Page 4131, line 5, 4131, line 5, then line 6 and 7, and then some discussion arose and then on the next page, line 10, you ruled on that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I see another one, Mr. Wladimiroff. Look on page 4136, line 28. That may be another concern you want to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is the one I referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Line 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You also referred to 4131 and page 4132, OK, and then page 4136.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it relates to the same matter. Two principles here, where your ruling on 4132 dealing with questions and your ruling you repeated that to handing out material. These rulings, if they stand, we have a problem with W.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I wanted to make sure, as I say, I did not hear you say 4136, but if you said it, I missed you, but I do see the ruling on 4131, 4132 and 4136, but they do relate to the same issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So that is the issue that we have asked for a briefing on and oral arguments. This morning you have indicated you are not ready to go forward. We will consider it Tuesday. That ruling will be withdrawn pending receipt of the material and oral argument and then a ruling after we have the benefit of all of those authorities. Does that satisfy you?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. You can go forward with W then?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Indeed we can.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. I am not sure, my understanding was that the Court was to sit on Monday, and I am not sure that was ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, we had planned on meeting next week Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday and the following week, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. We have one courtroom and we are just using it to our fullest. Thank you for cooperating but, yes, we did plan on meeting on Monday. Will you, lawyers, be able to or will you need the time for research?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am afraid not, we need that working day.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine, Mr. Wladimiroff. We have been trying to move along and I understand the problems you have had with your witnesses. I am trying to now help you, but since this issue has arisen, if you need the time, we will not receive any evidence on Monday. However that impacts on the witnesses, you will have to resolve. So Tuesday morning at 10 o'clock on that issue. Mr. Wladimiroff, the Prosecutor has provided a list of authorities and they have also provided us with a copy of the authorities. We will ask that you do the same for the Chamber. Would you do that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, we received that copy five minutes before we arrived here.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The authorities that you file in support of your position, provide us with a copy of the authorities as well. Would you do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I will, your Honour, but we may have problems having all materials translated. For example, the Dutch material, I gather, is all in Dutch, you see.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: That is understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I can understand, I hope you can through assistance of others, but I am not able to have it translated in due time.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you provide us with a copy of the materials? If you are having problems with the translation of materials, let us know, but please make your best effort to provide us because we can only read it, obviously, if it is in our language. I understand the problem you have. Do the best you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We will give you what we may gather. If we are able to have it translated, we will do, otherwise we will give it to you in the original language.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. You may do that, but please provide us copies of the supporting material. That is what we wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, we will, we certainly will. Your Honour, when we continue after this argument, I will leave the room because I have to take steps to provide for a change of our witnesses because we have to tell the Witness Unit that things might change next week.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I want you to do that so we will not have any problems. That is very helpful. Is there anything else because then we will have to stand in recess for five minutes so we can go back into closed session. Is there anything else, Mr. Niemann, Mr. Wladimiroff? No? Very good. We will stand in recess for five minutes and then return to closed session and the following witness will be in closed as well.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 22 23 24 25 26 27 28 Witness L, recalled.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. L, you understand that you are still under the oath that you took a few weeks ago to tell the truth, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Witness L, you remember when you last attended this courtroom you drew on a plan indicating various places around Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Do you remember indicating on that document where a place was that you called the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have noticed from the list of exhibits, in fact, that it is not on the official list that I have here. I wonder if anyone can help us with this matter, to know whether it has just been missed out in relation to a number or whether there has been an error of some sort?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Judge Vohrah said it was marked as D34.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we can call for that? I am grateful to Judge Vohrah for helping us on that matter. Can we have D34 and put that on the overhead projector? No, that is the wrong file. It should be Defence Exhibit file 34 and D38. Mr. Usher, if you would put No. 34 on the overhead projector and let the witness see it? Perhaps if we could have the picture back a bit, so that we get all of the picture on? That is fine, thank you. [To the witness]: Do you recollect telling us, Witness L, that the place where you marked an X in a circle was where you told us the white house in Trnopolje was situated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This was a house that you told us was the scene of a number of rapes committed by you and others, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: And where killings took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like to now show a video film of the road between the camp and those houses at Trnopolje. I would like you to identify as the camera goes up the road which of those houses you say was the white house. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If the technical booth could put on the first part of D61?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This is in evidence, I presume, Mr. Kay? What is the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is D61 which the Defence have just taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. If you could look at this film, Witness L, and as it moves up the road indicate to us which building is the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This road is leading to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And the building is on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And, according to this video tape, as far as I can see, you can only see the cultural centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You will see more of the film, Witness L.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You see the store. This is the dom or cultural centre, the white building. This is the store where the two cars are. This is the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could stop the video machine there? Which of those buildings shown on that film were or which building was the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot see it on this video tape. It is not recorded. It is not taped.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. If it is not on that video tape, in relation to those buildings that were photographed, whereabouts would that house have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, in relation to the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. You have marked it on your map, on the plan, and would you like to see the film again and indicate to us whereabouts in relation to the buildings of the camp the film should stop because at that point at some distance, no matter how far from the road, you would find the white house?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I had not seen this video before, so it was difficult for me to know what to expect, but I really am having some difficulty in understanding why this is new and why it is something that could not have been foreseen. I mean, the Defence have been in possession of the statement of the witness. The mention of the white house arises in that statement on numerous occasions. We know that the Defence have been to the scene. I would have expected that it would not have been too difficult to foresee, that a video taken of this scene by the Defence before the commencement of the trial would not have been possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would the Court like to hear me on this matter?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Because in fact there was no -- could the witness take his earphones off, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If the witness could put his headphones back on? Witness, what I want you to do is to call for the film to be stopped in the location off the road opposite that camp at Trnopolje where you say this building can be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You drew a map and made your mark on a map. I want you to stop the film when the camera gets to the point on the right where this building can be found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you stop there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just stop here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Or turn it back a little bit, back to the road. That is it. This is the road that you can see here, if you can zoom on it, just to see this like a small bridge, a path.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could just hold the camera for the moment? We see the road in our picture on the right-hand side of the screen, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The small path you are indicating, is that on the left-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, on the right when you are going from the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Perhaps if you could just indicate on your screen and if two of the lawyers -- is the magic pencil working -- can go and see where you are indicating, with your Honours' leave, so that we may identify this?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. You want to go, Mr. Kay and Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here is the road towards the white house, the school cannot be seen otherwise it can normally, but now you cannot see it. This is the main road going to the white house.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The two of you will now have to agree on what you saw and tell us for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The witness indicated on the right-hand side of the screen. Your Honour will see on the road what appears to be a change in colour. It goes from pinkish to brownish. If one moves one's finger to the right where there are some greenery in the general area of there, I wonder if Mr. Niemann would agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. It is not easy to describe, but the thing is that it is not right in the foreground. It is, in fact, looking at the film, about what seems to be between 10 and 15 metres down there is a change in colour of the road. So you have the road there, about 10 or 15 metres down there is a change in colour in the road. Where that change in colour of the road is, there is, in fact, on the screen a white spot in the greenery. It is about at that point.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: On the right-hand side here?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are we all pointing? Yes, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I do not think the white spot indicates the white house or anything. That is just an indication of the spot where the ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: It is a lighter spot than the greenery around it. I cannot tell and, of course, he cannot zoom in on it. He can only show what is photographed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think the rest of the film may take us to the place. Witness L, as the camera proceeds, can you tell us when we get to the location? If the technical booth could now play the film, perhaps slowly? (Video tape continued to be played)

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Would you stop the picture? Stop the picture? [No translation] You see the bridge, and along that path you reach the white house.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We are saying, the Judges are saying, we do not see a bridge. I see what looks like a discoloration on the right, a lighter colour, but I have no idea. If we go down further with the film, will we see anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, we will. Perhaps if the film now can be played in slow motion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There is a pillar. This is the fence. This is in the direction of the school which is behind. This is the school. This part that you can see now -- stop the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Stop the film, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So there is a big electric pylon. This used to be where the guardpost was. You can see No. 4 and across the road there is a little bridge and across that little bridge is the path leading to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Could it be played again in slow motion continuing up the road, perhaps a little bit faster than that, if it is possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here you can see the school.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this going forward?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Did you mean play again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, I meant go up the road. In fact, it is the camera moving to the left, your Honour. It is not going backwards. It is the movement of the camera.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: That is where we stopped before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You can see the little bridge here, not far -- as this film was taken you come out of the school ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just stop the camera there, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- and move.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just stop the film there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The white house is in this direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Continue with the film, please, at ordinary speed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also, here is this path that you can see branching off the road. Here, this last house that is here, below it to the left was the school. This is as you look from the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Stop there. Can you take the film back a bit, please? Just stop there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is difficult with this camera in the way this was shot. It is difficult to show it, to explain it. As for my showing it, I can show it, no problem about that, but on the basis of this footage it is a little bit difficult to understand, to understand where the white house was precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The bridge that you indicated, if you cross that bridge, that is the view that you would see, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cross the bridge and then you see a road, a path, which leads to the white house and you can see the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you help me with this? On the plans that you drew on when you gave evidence -- just look at D34.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Look to your right, please, Witness L. It is on the screen for you. Perhaps it can be put properly on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: It needs to move up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. [To the witness]: You see where that X is with a circle, just stop there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You placed the white house opposite at the end of the school building, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The little bridge you have indicated to us is, in fact, a little bridge opposite where your guardpost would have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we can have more of the map now shown on the screen because you put a No. 4 where your guardpost was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You did not mark opposite your guardpost, did you, Witness L?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guardpost No. 4 is this, and you can see the white house here. This, here is the office. Here is a small bridge which passes over and which we used to reach the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The little bridge you have indicated, Witness L, was opposite your guardpost at the end of the camp? Perhaps you would like to look at another map that you drew on, D38, please? If that could be put on the screen? If that can be taken back a little bit, please -- move the map up the screen a bit -- so we can see the bottom of the map? Just stop there. You wrote on this plan in red biro. This time you did a square and you did a track in red, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the white house. This here is where the command was, and this is the path leading to the white house. There is this little bridge which one otherwise used to come out of the camp, that is, this is the road for Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: When you drew on this plan you put that square indicating the white house again opposite the end of the school, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: We have just moved up that lane and passed the school and you did not indicate a white house opposite the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me, your cassette, the one that you shot, it is very difficult to show it to you, and mine -- had I drawn it with my own hand and brought it here to the Court during those two months that I was in the camp, then I would have indicated where the white house was, where the road was and all. This was a map that was brought here, put before me. I did not draw it. But, otherwise I can also see on this map where the school is, where the dom is, where the shop is and the road leading to Kozarac and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I would like you to see another section of film which was taken from where your guardpost was where you marked 4 on that map. If the second part of D61 could now be shown? If you could switch on to the video monitor? This is your guardpost, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Excuse me. I do not see any picture here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think you did see a picture before that. Is that where your guardpost was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No picture here, sorry. You can show me the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, the school is on the left.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the left. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is that where your guardpost No. 4 was at the corner of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we show the rest of the second section then of tape two?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think that is the second part of the first tape, 61. Do you have another Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will just sort the matter out. Whilst we are waiting, that house opposite your guardpost was a red house, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The house that you could see across the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where the command was. This house here that you see, it belongs to a man who lives there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just stop it there, please. Just stop it and back a bit, thank you. If we could move it back a bit, a couple of frames -- on a little bit. Thank you. You just hold it there. [To the witness]: That is the place then opposite guardpost 4 with the little bridge across the ditch that you indicated from that first film we showed you going up the road outside Trnopolje, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Kozarac, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Where would the white house be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind these houses here, a little further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is a red house that we can see part of in this picture.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is where the command headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What do you mean by "command headquarters"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, "command" to me, it means the one who is the main, the chief Commander of the camp and who came to guardposts. That was the headquarters of the Commander who was the principal for this job of the police, of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: That was in the actual camp itself, was it not, Witness L, in an office in the dom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was in this building. It is outside the camp. This command headquarters was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: In relation to this red building, where would we find the white house? Come on. You can tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was not very far away from this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can you help me a little bit more as to how far away from this house, if I was to walk behind this house where I would find it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Omarska about 250 metres or, as the crow flies, about 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we could let this film continue then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Could I just ask a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Witness, are you saying -- stop the film -- that this is the path that leads to the white house, and do I understand you as saying it is 100 or 150 metres up this path and I think from your diagram to the left, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So perhaps then before the film starts again, if we were to walk over this bridge and walk beside the red house, where would we go to find the white house, and how far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You go in the direction and in that direction is the white house. You move towards Omarska and you go for about 250 metres. Naturally, as you come -- as you move along that road you begin to see the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I do not want to begin to see the white house, I wanted to know where the white house was. You have told us it was 150 metres away. Now you are saying when we pass this red building, you walk ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: But as the crow flies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: --- towards Omarska and then you walk for 250 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, if you come out of the school from the main -- so you pass by the school, you come out, you walk past the office, and you start walking towards Omarska, in the direction of Omarska, to this white house and it is then on the right-hand side but in the direction of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Can you reorientate our minds, where would Omarska be?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I will ask the witness, your Honour. If we could have the film back on? Where would Omarska be if we cross this bridge and walked beside the red house in the photograph? In which direction would we be walking to get to Omarska, as you describe it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, on the right-hand side you walk one or, perhaps, two kilometres to Omarska. You can also go through the railway station, turn towards Kozarac and then use the main road, Banja Luka/Prijedor, that is, and you reach Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, we are not going through the railway station. We are going across this small ditch, across the bridge and we are walking past that red house. Do we keep walking in a straight line or do we turn in any other direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You go straight ahead and you come to the white house. There is no way to divert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. So we do not turn to the left and we do not turn to the right. We just keep walking straight across that ditch and we get to the white house, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: For how far would we walk from that bridge to get to that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you, from the school, as far as I could judge, when I walked it would be about 250 metres normally, as you walk normally, and as the crow flies it is less. Of course, if a crow flies then, of course, it is one thing, and if you walk on the ground then it is a little longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we could continue with the film then in relation to what can be seen around this area? If the booth could play the film at a normal speed? Actually just stop the film here. Why can we not see the white house from your guardpost? Can you take the film back, please? If we can move the film back to the previous shot? Why can we not see the white house from your guardpost? Just hold it there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, from what I can see, there are trees here. Then there is this building and this foliage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But you told us that you could see it from your guardpost and it is across this bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, it has been four years and more since I worked at the camp, but when I was there you could see the white house from my guardpost. I am telling the truth that that building was visible from my guardpost, and my guardpost can also be seen from the white house. This here that was filmed, I do not know when it was, what month it was, when this film was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we could continue with the film then? That is a scene of the road that ran alongside the Trnopolje camp, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is again the position of your guardpost with the school some distance to your right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This road that we now see was not there. Many things were not there when I was there, from what I can see on the film.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This road has always been there, has it not? It is the road to Kozarac railway station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could be that road, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we just stop the camera here? Here is a white house quite near the water pump. Can you see that water pump?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Did you mean this house as the white house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let the camera continue. If we can just stop the film here, thank you, and switch the television monitor off? Your Honour, it might be an appropriate moment to take a break at this time now for the Defence to look at some material which might help us to develop this matter in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I am much obliged, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Witness L, I would like you to watch a third section of film now and if the technical booth could play the third section of this Exhibit 61? So, video monitors on. (The video was played). This is the rear of that building that was a white house opposite the school. Indicate to us, whilst the camera moves around to the rear countryside, if you can tell us where the white house is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is the one opposite the school that we were looking at the front of it before the break. This is the area directly behind that red house and that white house opposite the school. Can you tell us where this white house is, if we can see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This does not look familiar. I do not know this. I can just show where the school is and in relation to the school where the building was, but this does not look familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: This is the whole area behind that white house and red house situated by the road. You see now we travel down the side of this building, come out opposite the school, and there is the water pump, the front of this house, there is the school, there are the trees, there is the road.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you stop there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the school over there, and up here is the red house and behind that red house there is a path leading to the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let the film continue and we will play it again from the beginning. All the camera has done has been in a circle around this white house.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay, pretty soon I am going to ask you to take the oath, but it has been in a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Sorry, your Honour. Yes. I do not mean to state the obvious to the Court. I am sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: No, actually it was not obvious to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If we stop there as this is the interior of that white house? If we can go back to the beginning again to give you another chance to look at it. Just so it is clear, just stop there -- no, back a bit please. If you take it a few frames back? Stop there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where this electric post is, that was my guardpost, where this electric pillar is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Right. Let us play the film again and you tell us, as the camera takes us around the area, where the white house would be found and tell the camera to stop, the film to stop. So if you could play it again, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the red house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is where the command was. This building was not there. Would you go back a little, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: If you could go back a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Behind this red house is the path leading to the white house, towards the white house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Let us continue to play it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the red house. Behind the red house, you pass there and you go in the direction of Omarska and straight ahead is the white house. This is not it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: There is the red house on the right. This is the area behind the red house.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, but on this video film I cannot show you where the house is. I was there in the winter, so everything was ----

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Stop there, please. It seems, does it not, that we cannot see this white house, certainly from the back of the white house and red house that we have been looking at, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: You told us this was a building you could see from your guardpost?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: From that position you said that you could see things happening there, such as the killing of men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you could see the pole. You could see the people. You could see the white house normally, but I was there in winter time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. I do not require the use of the video monitor any more. When you worked as a guard at Trnopolje, you told us that you were promised 300 marks a month as your wages for working at the camp, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Again, your Honour, I object to this question ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: --- due to the fact that it is not a new matter. It was a matter that was raised in the course of the evidence-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: This may be a preliminary question. Let us see where we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could be allowed to ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes, I will overrule the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Thank you. [To the witness]: You told us that you were not paid that money, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So how were you surviving, how was your family getting money?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My mother was working in a company and my father was called up and he had a military pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: I think you told us that your father died and that you attended his funeral?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Presumably, after your father died there was no money coming from him, is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but there is my mother.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there anyone else at home who was working?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was working. After '93 I was working in agriculture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: No, I am talking about in 1992 whilst you are at Trnopolje. You told us your mother was working for a company. Was that whilst you were working at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, afterwards, after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: But during this time that you are a guard at Trnopolje, from the end of October to the end of December, was your mother working then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but my father was on the front. Then he got killed. I was in the camp working, but I never got any money and I was a guard there and I was supposed to get compensation. I did not get compensation, and then I ran away from that camp, not to work there any more, because I could not stand it and they gave me drugs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Was there anyone else at home who was able to work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I only had a mother and a sister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: So it was just your mother, your sister and you at home, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Would you just like to look at this photograph and tell me if you recognise this man? (Handed). Do you recognise that man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: It is not your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: What was your father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Is your father not alive today ----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I object, your Honour, to questions that may lead to the identification of the family based on the order that the Court made in this regard and matters which may tend to identify.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the particular person of the family is, apparently, dead and the witness has given the name of that person, so there does not appear to be any harm that could occasion in relation to this questioning. When the court made this particular order -- I refer to paragraph 15 of the Court's judgment -- can the witness take his headphones off, please, and perhaps the witness withdraw from court?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Sir, would you take your headphones off -- put your headphones back on. Do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you understand English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there an indication otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would feel much happier if the witness was not in court. I am sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I understand -- OK. I will ask the witness to go out. Remember now, we are trying to proceed as expeditiously as possible and not be too technical. Take your earphones off, sir. Take your earphones off. We agreed that the process would be that the witnesses would take their earphones off. Now you are telling me you want him to go out of court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Your Honour, in most circumstances, I would approach the Court on that basis as I have done, but here I am dealing particularly with sensitive matters and the Defence have good reason here in the questioning that is being undertaken.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Mr. Usher, would you take the witness out?

procedural_notes.text: (The Court adjourned for a short time)
(Hearing in closed session – released by Trial Chamber II on 18 August 1997)
(The Court adjourned for a short time)
